---
title: "Expression Execution"
---

The `marrow/expr` module provides a lazy expression system for building and executing query plans. Expressions compose into a plan tree of immutable `Relation` nodes; calling `.execute()` on a plan opens it into a pull-based processor tree that streams `RecordBatch` results. The plan itself is never mutated, so it is a reusable template.

::: {.callout-note}
The examples on this page use the Mojo `marrow.expr` API. They illustrate the
native expression layer rather than the Python bindings.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "../../python")
import marrow as ma
```

## Building expressions

### Column references and literals

`col(name)` references a column by name. `lit(value)` wraps a scalar constant.

```python
from marrow.expr import col, lit

age  = col("age")
name = col("name")
threshold = lit(30)
```

### Operator overloads

Expression nodes support the standard operators, which compose into larger nodes:

| Operator | Expression node |
|----------|----------------|
| `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` | `Binary(ADD / SUB / MUL / DIV)` |
| `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, `==`, `!=` | `Binary(GT / LT / GE / LE / EQ / NE)` |
| `&`, `\|` | `Binary(AND / OR)` |
| `-expr` | `Unary(NEG)` |
| `~expr` | `Unary(NOT)` |

```python
adults    = col("age") > lit(30)
cheap     = col("price") <= lit(100)
qualified = adults & cheap
```

### `if_else`

Element-wise conditional: `if_else(condition, true_value, false_value)`.

```python
from marrow.expr import if_else

label = if_else(col("score") >= lit(90), lit("pass"), lit("fail"))
```

### `is_null` and `cast`

```python
from marrow.expr import col

missing = col("optional_field").is_null()
as_f64  = col("price").cast(ma.float64())
```

## Relational plan nodes

Plan nodes represent transformations on tabular data. They are composed via chaining.

### InMemoryTable

`in_memory_table(batch)` wraps a `RecordBatch` as a leaf node.

```python
from marrow.expr import in_memory_table

batch = ma.record_batch(
    [ma.array([25, 35, 45, 20]), ma.array(["Alice", "Bob", "Carol", "Dave"])],
    names=["age", "name"],
)
source = in_memory_table(batch)
```

### ParquetScan

`parquet_scan(path)` reads a Parquet file lazily — the file is read when the plan is executed, not when the node is constructed.

```python
from marrow.expr import parquet_scan

source = parquet_scan("employees.parquet")
```

### Filter

`.filter(predicate)` keeps rows where the boolean expression is `True`. Null rows are excluded.

```python
adults = source.filter(col("age") > lit(30))
```

### Project

`.select(*names)` keeps a subset of columns by name (projection of computed
expressions is not yet available through `select`):

```python
projected = adults.select("name", "age")
```

### Aggregate

`.aggregate(keys, values, funcs)` groups by the key columns and applies the
named aggregate functions to the value columns.

```python
totals = source.aggregate(["dept"], ["salary"], ["sum"])
```

## Executing a plan

`plan.execute()` opens the plan into a fresh pull-based processor tree, drains
it, and returns a single `RecordBatch`. It is a method on the plan, not a free
function. A plan is a pure description, so it can be executed repeatedly and
concurrently. An optional `ExecContext` selects the execution mode:

```python
from marrow.execution import ExecContext

result = plan.execute()                  # serial by default
result = plan.execute(ExecContext())     # explicit context
```

`ExecContext` comes from `marrow.execution` and offers
`.serial()`, `.parallel()` and `.gpu(device)` constructors — see
[GPU acceleration](gpu.qmd).

## End-to-end example

```python
from marrow.expr import col, lit, in_memory_table

# Source data
batch = ma.record_batch(
    [
        ma.array([25, 35, 45, 20, 55]),
        ma.array(["Alice", "Bob", "Carol", "Dave", "Eve"]),
        ma.array([70_000, 90_000, 110_000, 50_000, 130_000]),
    ],
    names=["age", "name", "salary"],
)

# Build a plan: keep employees over 30 with salary > 80k, return name + salary
plan = (
    in_memory_table(batch)
    .filter((col("age") > lit(30)) & (col("salary") > lit(80_000)))
    .select("name", "salary")
)

# Execute — returns a single RecordBatch
result = plan.execute()
print(result)
```

## Reading from Parquet

Plans that scan Parquet files work identically. The file is read on demand
during execution, and a `.filter` above a `parquet_scan` pushes its predicate
into the scan so row groups and pages can be pruned using the file's
statistics.

```python
from marrow.expr import col, lit, parquet_scan

plan = (
    parquet_scan("employees.parquet")
    .filter(col("age") > lit(30))
    .select("name", "age")
)

result = plan.execute()
```
